text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

Thanks for reaching out — I'll facilitate this for the three of you and keep a shared list of concerns so nothing gets lost. I'm not deciding anything and can't move money or give legal advice.

Starting point: I'll ask each of you one question.

For you: what matters to you about the trailer, and why? Not what you want to happen — what's the thing underneath it that you'd want me to get right.
I need the trailer available for my home project in the next few weeks. I need to be able to use it, not just wait until A’s finished.

Hi A — C asked me to help the three of you sort out the cargo trailer you bought together. I'm just the facilitator: I keep a shared list of what each person needs, and I don't decide anything or move money.

To start: what matters to you about the trailer, and why? Not the plan you want — the thing underneath it that you'd want me to get right.
I want the freedom to take the trailer on my weekend trips without having to negotiate each use. I’m hoping to start within the next few weeks.

Hi B — C asked me to help the three of you sort out the cargo trailer you bought together. I'm just the facilitator: I keep a shared list of what each person needs, and I don't decide anything or move money.

I understand your pad is where the trailer lives, which may put you in an awkward spot. To start: what matters to you about the trailer, and why? Not the plan you want — the thing underneath it that you'd want me to get right.
I’d like the trailer not to be in the way on my pad. I did go along with keeping it here, though, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming anyone.

That's useful. Let me try to put it in plain words and you tell me if it fits:

Entry 1 — "C wants to be able to count on getting real use of the trailer for their own project, on a timetable they can plan around, rather than their plans depending on when someone else is done."

Does that fit? If a word is off, say which. (And if there's something more underneath — say, being treated as an equal owner, or not being the one who always yields — tell me and I'll add it.)
Yes, that fits. Underneath it, I need some freedom to plan and use the trailer for my own project, not have my plans depend on someone else’s schedule.

Thank you — and noted that you're not looking to blame anyone. Let me try to put it in plain words and you tell me if it fits:

Entry 2 — "B wants her own space to stay usable and unblocked, so having the trailer there doesn't cost her the use of her pad."

Does that fit? If a word is off, say which. And if there's more underneath — e.g. not wanting to be the one who has to police it, or not wanting to be in the middle between A and C — tell me and I'll add it.

Mostly, yes. I’d like the pad clear, though I feel a bit awkward asking since I agreed to keep it there. I’d also need to check with my landlord before changing what’s kept on the pad; I haven’t asked him yet.

Thanks — that's clear. Here's the list so far, so you can see it:

1. C — wants to be able to count on real use of the trailer for their own project, on a timetable they can plan around, rather than their plans depending on someone else's schedule. (CONFIRMED by C)

2. B — wants her pad to stay clear and usable, so keeping the trailer there doesn't cost her the use of her own space. (not yet confirmed — B said "mostly"; wording being rechecked)

A hasn't given me their words yet; I've asked.

One more thing on your entry: you mentioned wanting "freedom to plan and use" it. Do you also want that freedom to be something you can rely on without checking in each time — or is checking in fine as long as it's predictable? Either answer is useful; I just want the entry to say what you actually mean.
I’d like a predictable arrangement I can rely on, without having to renegotiate each time.

Here's the list so far, so you can see it:

1. C — wants to be able to count on real use of the trailer for their own project, on a timetable they can plan around, rather than their plans depending on someone else's schedule. (confirmed by C)

2. B — wants her pad to stay clear and usable, so keeping the trailer there doesn't cost her the use of her own space. (not yet confirmed — wording being rechecked with B)

Yours isn't written up yet — I want your words first. From your message I'd try:

3. A — "A wants the freedom to use the trailer for weekend trips without having to negotiate each use."

Does that fit? If it's not quite right, tell me which words are off. And if there's more underneath — e.g. not wanting to be the one who always has to ask — say so and I'll add it.
Yes, that fits. Freedom to use it without having to ask or negotiate each time is the point.

Good — that sharpens it. Revised:

1. C — wants a predictable arrangement they can rely on to use the trailer for their own project in the next few weeks, without having to renegotiate each time. Confirmed by C.

Does the revised wording still fit? (I'll record it only when you say yes.)

I'm rechecking B's wording now, and A's isn't confirmed yet. Once all three are, I'll draft some options that meet all of them and bring them back to you — you'll each get a chance to say no to anything before it counts as settled.
Yes, that fits.

Thanks for flagging the landlord part — that's a real constraint, and I don't want the plan to assume something we haven't checked. I'll note it as its own item rather than blending it in.

Revised wording for yours:

2. B — wants her pad to stay clear and usable, so keeping the trailer there doesn't cost her the use of her own space.

2a. B — needs to check with her landlord before anything changes about what's kept on the pad; not yet asked.

Does 2 fit as written? And if it's honest that you'd feel awkward, I can note that too — you're allowed to have a concern you agreed to earlier; "I went along with it then" doesn't make it not count now.

Current list:
1. C — predictable arrangement to use the trailer for their project in the next few weeks, without renegotiating each time. (confirmed by C, pending re-check of revised wording)
2. B — pad stays clear and usable. (not confirmed)
2a. B — landlord check needed before changing what's kept on the pad. (unresolved)
3. A — not yet written up; asked.
Yes, that fits. Please note I feel awkward asking, since I agreed to the arrangement and feel I owe A and C. I’d need my landlord’s approval before changing what’s kept on the pad.

List update — C's and B's are now confirmed:

1. C — wants a predictable arrangement they can rely on to use the trailer for their own project in the next few weeks, without having to renegotiate each time. CONFIRMED by C.

2. B — wants her pad to stay clear and usable, so keeping the trailer there doesn't cost her the use of her own space. CONFIRMED by B.

2a. B — feels awkward raising this, since she agreed to the arrangement and feels she owes A and C. Noted; it doesn't make the concern smaller.

2b. B — needs her landlord's approval before anything changes about what's kept on the pad. UNRESOLVED (landlord not yet asked).

Still outstanding: A's concern — I've asked A for their words and am waiting.

Nothing is settled until all three are on the list and you've all seen the options. I'll come back to you.
Understood. Please make sure the options include a predictable way for me to use it in the next few weeks.

Your entry is confirmed. Full list:

1. A — wants the freedom to use the trailer for weekend trips without having to ask or negotiate each use. CONFIRMED.
2. C — wants a predictable arrangement to use the trailer for their own project in the next few weeks, without renegotiating each time. CONFIRMED.
3. B — wants her pad to stay clear and usable, so the trailer there doesn't cost her the use of her own space. CONFIRMED.
3a. B — feels awkward raising it (she agreed earlier, feels she owes you both). Noted, not discounted.
3b. B — needs her landlord's approval before anything changes about what's kept on the pad. UNRESOLVED.

Draft options — all three aim to meet all of 1, 2, 3:

Option 1 — Fixed calendar blocks. You and C agree dates now, in advance, covering the next few weeks (and beyond). Each of you takes the trailer on your own blocks with no asking. Trailer returns to B's pad between uses and is parked in one defined spot she picks, so her pad stays usable.

Option 2 — Blocks plus off-pad storage. Same fixed blocks, but the trailer lives somewhere other than B's pad between uses (another spot, rented space, or your or C's place). B's pad fully clear; may cost money or need C's agreement — for you three to decide.

Option 3 — Blocks, and B's pad as a short-term stop only. Trailer sits on B's pad only briefly between uses, off-pad otherwise. Meets 3 most fully; needs somewhere to put it.

Two honest flags: 1 and 2 both need A and C to share the near-term weeks, and 3b means any option that changes what's on B's pad waits on her landlord.

Does anyone have even a minor discomfort with any of this — or a concern I haven't listed? A no or a small niggle is welcome; it tells me what to add, not what to argue with.
A concern: fixed blocks could limit spontaneous trips, though I’m willing to plan dates. I don’t want to commit to off-pad storage or any cost until we know the details.

Draft options, each aiming to meet all three:

Option 1 — Fixed calendar blocks. You and A agree dates now, in advance, covering the next few weeks. Each takes the trailer on their own blocks with no asking. Trailer returns to B's pad between uses, parked in one defined spot she picks.

Option 2 — Blocks plus off-pad storage. Same fixed blocks, but the trailer lives somewhere other than B's pad between uses. B's pad fully clear; may cost money — your call as owners.

Option 3 — Blocks, with B's pad as a brief stop only between uses. Meets B's concern most fully; needs another place to put it.

Honest flag on your priority: 1 and 2 both need you and A to share the near-term weeks, so neither can promise you the whole next few weeks. If that's a problem, tell me — it's information, not an objection.

Does anyone have even a minor discomfort — or something I've failed to list? Small niggles welcome.

My concern: “share the next few weeks” doesn’t guarantee enough time for my project. We need to agree actual dates and a usable block for me, not just assume a split works. No need for the whole period, but I can’t wait until A is done.

Your entry is confirmed, and thanks for naming the awkwardness — I've kept it on the list as its own line rather than tucking it away.

Full list:
1. C — predictable arrangement to use the trailer for their project in the next few weeks, no renegotiating each time. CONFIRMED.
2. A — freedom to use it for weekend trips without asking or negotiating each use. CONFIRMED.
3. B — pad stays clear and usable. CONFIRMED.
3a. B — feels awkward asking, since she agreed and feels she owes A and C. Noted, not discounted.
3b. B — needs landlord's approval before changing what's kept on the pad. UNRESOLVED.

Option 2 — Same blocks, but the trailer lives off B's pad between uses; her pad fully clear (may cost money).

Two things:
- If you'd rather the trailer not come back to your pad at all, say so — that's a legitimate need, not an imposition, even though you agreed earlier.
- Does anyone have even a minor discomfort, or something I haven't listed? Small niggles are welcome; a no tells me what to add.
I’d prefer it not come back to my pad between uses, if there’s a workable alternative. I do feel awkward saying that, and I’d need to ask my landlord before changing the arrangement.

Update — C and B both refined their concerns in response to the options. Current list:

1. C — wants a predictable arrangement to use the trailer for their own project in the next few weeks, without renegotiating each time. CONFIRMED. Refinement: needs actual agreed dates and a genuinely usable block, not an assumed split; doesn't need the whole period, but can't wait until A is done.
2. A — wants the freedom to use the trailer for weekend trips without asking or negotiating each use. CONFIRMED.
3. B — wants her pad to stay clear and usable. CONFIRMED. Refinement: would prefer the trailer not return to her pad between uses at all, if there's a workable alternative.
3a. B — feels awkward asking, since she agreed earlier and feels she owes you both. Noted, not discounted.
3b. B — needs her landlord's approval before anything changes about what's kept on the pad. UNRESOLVED.

What this means for the options: C's refinement rules out "we'll work it out". Any option now needs concrete dates agreed, with a real block for C in the next few weeks and A's weekends protected. B's refinement points toward off-pad storage between uses.

I need your reaction before anything is treated as settled, and I'd rather have it than guess:
- Is a fixed calendar with agreed dates workable for you, and roughly which weekends do you want?
- Would off-pad storage between uses be acceptable to you, or does the trailer need to be at yours or B's?

And: does anyone have even a minor discomfort, or something I haven't listed? A no is useful — it tells me what to add.

A fixed calendar is workable, but I can’t name weekends until I check my plans; I want some weekend time in the next few weeks. Off-pad storage is acceptable if I can access the trailer for my agreed dates without asking each time. I’d need to know the location and any cost before agreeing.
